wb.title: W + B
wb.sub:
Frozen writer teacher
Transfer image only

explanations: The same G generates random, reference-transfer and reconstruction words in one batched forward. D sees all three; R sees only random/transfer; W+B sees only transfer. The reference and canonical target x may have different widths.
L_D = E[(1 − D(x))₊] + (1/3) Σ_b E[(1 + D(stop(x_b)))₊] + L_R1,    b ∈ {rand, style, rec}.
L_adv = −(1/3) Σ_b E[D(x_b)];    L_CTC = λ_r CTC(R(x_rand), y′) + λ_s CTC(R(x_style), y′);    L_writer = CE(W(B(x_style)), w).
L_GE = L_adv + 0.45 L_adv,P + L_CTC + 0.5 L_writer + λ_rec L_rec + L_info + L_cycle + 0.02 L_content + 0.1 L_ctx + 0.1 L_KL.

D/P update every batch; G/E update every second critic batch. In the G/E phase, D/P/B/R/W parameters are frozen but input gradients remain. R and W+B are pretrained on real images; W+B starts from the OCR CNN. See (b)/(c) for the other losses.

Normal config: λ_r 1→0.4 (epochs 10–20), λ_s 0.5→0.20 (8–28), λ_rec 10→2.5 (24–42). Lazy R1 = (0.01 × 32 / 2) E||∇_x D(x)||² every 32 critic batches. D includes the same mild differentiable augmentation policy for real and fake.

content.title: Content BCE
content.sub:
GRL → learned probe
vs bag of characters in y

explanations: What is reconstructed — and what is not

Pixel L1 compares x_rec to the canonical real image x over valid pixels, not to the original-width style reference. Global information recovery reconstructs the prior z_g; transfer cycle recovers the reference global mean. These are separate targets, not three copies of one loss.
L_rec = mean_valid |x_rec − x|;    L_info = mean |E_g(B(x_rand)) − stop(z_g)| / 8;    L_cycle = mean |E_g(B(x_style)) − stop(mu_g,ref)| / 8.
L_KL = KL[N(mu_g, diag(exp(logvar_g))) || N(0,I)] / 8;    g = mu_g + exp(0.5 logvar_g) ⊙ ε;    ε ∼ N(0,I);    ℓ_g = log σ_g².
L_content = balanced-BCE(Probe(GRL(mu_g,ref)), bag(y)) / 8;    GRL is identity forward and reverses only the gradient toward E.

The probe learns reference character presence while E is pushed to hide it in g. Local L is a deterministic, centered 7-token residual; it is neither KL-regularized nor reconstructed against random local slots. E_g skips local retrieval. All repeated B/E/G blocks share weights.

These three generated branches also receive the global and patch adversarial losses in (a)/(c). Only x_rand and x_style receive OCR CTC. The /8 factors preserve the explicit eight-token normalization implemented in the current loss functions.

ctx.title: CTX
ctx.sub:
Fake B maps vs
stop(reference B maps)

explanations: One crop policy; two complementary supervision signals

Crop side s = H/2 (16 at H32, 32 at H64). Horizontal start positions are stratified; vertical locations alternate upper/lower halves. Real and all fake branches use the same policy, not identical coordinates. Only P receives these crops; global D always receives complete words.
K_n = clamp(ceil(W_n / (H/2)), 4, 8);    L_P = HingeMap(P(C(x)), +1) + (1/3) Σ_b HingeMap(P(C(stop(x_b))), −1).
L_adv,P = −(1/3) Σ_b MeanWord[MeanCrop[MeanMap[P(C(x_b))]]];    generator contribution = 0.45 L_adv,P.
L_ctx = Σ_l CX(stop(B_l(x_ref)), B_l(x_style));    generator contribution = 0.1 L_ctx;    l ∈ {three selected backbone scales}.

P: 3×3 stem (1→64) → three residual StrokePatchBlocks (128→192→192; 3×3 plus axial DW 1×5 / 5×1 and 1×1 fusion) → spatial logit head. Pooling preserves a minimum 4×4 grid. Hinge is applied BEFORE map/crop reduction, then each word and fake branch is weighted equally.

CTX matches non-aligned multiscale writer features to new text, with at most 256 sampled spatial features per comparison. Cached B maps are reused. The context comparison is not a reconstruction pixel target, frequency loss, foreground mask or independent texture-refinement network.

out.title: Generated image x_rand
out.sub:
H × (character_width × T)
No D, P, R or writer classifier

explanations: Text establishes spatial content before local style is injected. The same style layout is used by random and reference-guided generation: one global token for block-wide conditioning and seven centered local tokens for spatial appearance. No character-specific fallback or single-digit switch is used.
z_g ∼ N(0, I_32);    Z_L ∼ N(0, I) with shape 7 × 32;    L_j = Z_L,j − (1/7) Σ_k Z_L,k;    x_rand = G([z_g,L], y′).
Spatial refinement: Q = W_Q LN(F);    K = W_K LN(L);    V = W_V L;    F_out = F + α ⊙ W_O Attention(Q,K,V).

Content attention and spatial style attention each use 4 heads and attention width 128. Spatial style refinement happens once after the first GBlock. α is learned per feature channel (initialized at 0.25), not a hardcoded character gate.

Both native heights retain four GBlocks (512→256→128→64→64 channels). Feature heights are 4→8→16→32→32 at H32, or 4→8→16→32→64 at H64. The final stage refines at constant resolution or upsamples according to requested geometry.
T = valid target character count;    output width = 16T at H32 or 32T at H64.    Inference: no loss, backward pass or critic optimizer step.

out.title: Styled output
out.sub:
x_style = G(S_ref, y′)
Reference writer appearance

explanations: A learned global/local representation, not a reference-length rule

B supplies multiscale visual evidence. E separates global pooled style from local residual evidence. During deterministic evaluation, g = mu_g; the seven local tokens are always deterministic. Reference text labels and writer IDs are not inputs to this inference path.
g = mu_g(B(x_ref));    L = CenterSlots[W_out Attention(Q_learned, K_visual+2Dposition, V_visual−valid_mean)];    S_ref = [g,L] ∈ R^(8×32).
x_style = G(S_ref, y′);    if y′ = y and the target geometry matches the training reconstruction target, this becomes the reconstruction path.

The global branch uses two residual gated DW k7 context blocks with dilations 1 and 2. Local evidence uses three B scales pooled to four height rows, projected to 256 channels, and queried by seven orthogonally initialized learned slots with four attention heads. Positions address evidence through K; they are not added to appearance V.

Configured GAN sampling/evaluation uses EMA G/E (beta 0.9998) and fixed pretrained B. W, R, D and P are unnecessary for generation. FID/KID/HWD are downstream measurements, not inputs to this graph or objectives backpropagated during evaluation.

Shared notation: x_ref = original reference geometry; x = canonical real reconstruction target; y = its transcript; y′ = requested text; w = training writer ID. The diagrams summarize normal gan_iam_32/64 configurations, not MAIN’s separate token-capacity experiment.
